definitions.explanation: Describes something extremely rare or unusual in occurrence. Carries a formal, literary tone and is often used to emphasize just how exceptional something is.

examples.japanese: {稀有|けう}な{才能|さいのう}の{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}だ。
こんな{経験|けいけん}は{稀有|けう}なことだ。
examples.english: An experience like this is truly rare.

examples.japanese: {世界的|せかいてき}にも{稀有|けう}な{自然環境|しぜんかんきょう}が、この{島|しま}には{残|のこ}されている。
examples.english: A natural environment rare even by world standards remains on this island.

notes:
USAGE:
Functions as a na-adjective ({稀有|けう}な). This is a formal, literary word — in everyday conversation, {珍|めずら}しい is far more common. {稀有|けう} is chosen when the speaker wants to emphasize how truly exceptional something is.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {稀有|けう}な{才能|さいのう}: rare talent
- {稀有|けう}な{存在|そんざい}: a rare existence
- {稀有|けう}な{例|れい}: a rare case
- {稀有|けう}な{体験|たいけん}: a rare experience

READING NOTE:
Also sometimes read きゆう, but けう is the standard modern reading.

SIMILAR WORDS:
{珍|めずら}しい is the everyday word for "rare" or "unusual." {稀有|けう} is more elevated and emphasizes extraordinary rarity. {希少|きしょう} means "scarce" and is used more for resources, species, and quantities.
